title: Species Recovery: Cheetah, Bustard, Gharial, Snow Leopard

cards.b:
UPSC asks which project belongs to which animal, which state, which IUCN status. Current affairs, like the cheetah translocation, push these species into Prelims and Mains.

Treat each species as a small card: status, place, project, threat.

Status words matter: one word, such as Critically Endangered versus Vulnerable, often decides a Prelims option.

The Asiatic cheetah was declared extinct in India in 1952. Under Project Cheetah, eight African cheetahs from Namibia were brought to Kuno National Park, Madhya Pradesh, on 17 September 2022. Twelve more came from South Africa in February 2023. Gandhi Sagar sanctuary was prepared as a second site.

The African cheetah is a different subspecies from the Asiatic cheetah, which survives only in Iran. IUCN: cheetah is Vulnerable. Early deaths of several animals raised doubts about the site's space and prey.

The great Indian bustard (GIB) is Critically Endangered. Most live in Rajasthan (Desert National Park, Jaisalmer), with small groups in Gujarat, Maharashtra, Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh. It is Rajasthan's state bird, Schedule I of the WPA, and was a candidate for India's national bird in the 1960s.

Main threat: overhead power lines that cause collisions. In April 2021 the Supreme Court ordered underground cables in priority areas. Breeding centres at Jaisalmer try to raise chicks. The 2024 order eased the strict ruling and set a balance with renewable energy.

The gharial is a fish-eating crocodilian, Critically Endangered. The main breeding population is in the National Chambal Sanctuary (Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh). Project Crocodile began in 1975 to protect gharial, mugger and saltwater crocodile.

Threats: sand mining, dams and irrigation canals, fishing nets and river pollution. Chambal also supports the Gangetic dolphin and the red-crowned roof turtle.

The snow leopard is listed Vulnerable. Its range in India covers Ladakh, Himachal, Uttarakhand, Sikkim and Arunachal. Project Snow Leopard (2009) uses a community model. The SECURE Himalaya project (UNDP-GEF, with MoEFCC) protects high-altitude landscapes. A first national assessment (2019-23) reported about 718 snow leopards (about 477 in Ladakh), a figure to verify before use.

Threats: retaliation killing for livestock, mining, climate-driven loss of snow.

• Project Dolphin (2020): Gangetic dolphin (National Aquatic Animal, 2009), Endangered. Vikramshila Gangetic Dolphin Sanctuary in Bihar.
  • Project Crocodile: 1975.
  • Vulture Action Plan (2006): ban on diclofenac; breeding at Pinjore (Haryana).
  • Project Hangul: Kashmir stag in Dachigam, Critically Endangered.
  • Sangai: brow-antlered deer at Keibul Lamjao, Manipur, on floating phumdis.
  • Project Elephant, Project Tiger, Project Lion (Asiatic lion in Gir).

Critics say India spent large funds on cheetahs while grassland species like the bustard and blackbuck lose range. Supporters say the cheetah is a flagship for restoring open grasslands. Some argue conservation should first shield habitat and then bring species back.

The IUCN has rules for translocation: check the cause of loss, habitat fit and community support.

Many of these species depend on neglected landscapes: grasslands, riverine sandbars and high-altitude meadows. Land records often call them "wasteland". Policy such as a National Grassland Mission or wise wetland use is needed. The Supreme Court has acted on several species, including the GIB.

Some ecologists also argue the cheetah project is not a recovery of the Asiatic cheetah, since India lacks that subspecies.

• Cheetah: Kuno, 2022; extinct 1952.
  • GIB: Critically Endangered; Rajasthan; power lines.
  • Gharial: Critically Endangered; Chambal; Project Crocodile 1975.
  • Snow leopard: Vulnerable; SECURE Himalaya.
  • Dolphin: Project Dolphin 2020.
  • Hangul: Dachigam.

Add the Great Indian Bustard Project at Jaisalmer and the Vulture Action Plan 2006 as extra rows.

Prelims-style: "Which species is the target of Project Hangul?" (Kashmir stag). "Where is the National Chambal Sanctuary?"

Mains-style: "Evaluate India's species recovery programmes, with special reference to the cheetah project." Structure: aim; method; early results; criticisms (space, prey, cost); lessons; alternatives (grassland protection).

Quote one criticism and one reform to show balance.
